_comment: AUTHORED. The scenarios and surfaces this corpus must carry. A scenario directory that goes missing, or a surface file that is not captured, fails a test rather than reading as a state nobody needed. Do not derive this from what is on disk — deriving it would make a silent deletion invisible, which is the whole failure it exists to catch.

scenarios.name: empty
scenarios.why: No rows at all — the degenerate path (design 1.1).

scenarios.name: metered-usage
scenarios.why: The ordinary path: two providers, several models, current-month and prior-month/7-day data. Not in design 1.1's list; added because that list exercises no single scenario covering summary, per-provider burn, trend, model breakdown, card ordering and report reconciliation together.

scenarios.name: subscriptions-only
scenarios.why: Money with no usage events (design 1.1; design 4.2 depends on this shape too).

scenarios.name: stale-cards
scenarios.why: stale_cards populated and newest_fetched_at old. Separate from incomplete-cards because the two fields are computed and rendered independently.

scenarios.name: incomplete-cards
scenarios.why: incomplete_card_count non-zero — the caveat surface has its own payload field.

scenarios.name: provider-filtered
scenarios.why: The ?provider= scope is a different code path from the portfolio view (design 1.1).

scenarios.name: two-currency
scenarios.why: The only multi-currency scenario. Two currencies with real spend, one card holding both (design 7.2), and a primary_currency that is NOT the larger spend — so the served 4.2 order is distinguishable from both alphabetical and size order, and each ring's percentages are provably a share of that ring rather than of a sum across currencies.

surfaces.why: GET /api/v1/dashboard/breakdown — carries the per-card and per-model cost_usd scalars, which 5 replaces with per-schema shapes.
GET /api/v1/report — carries total_usd and balance_total_usd, which 7.0 removes rather than restyles.

report_pdf.render_html() — the PDF's markup. The bytes are not goldened, but every scenario's report IS rendered to PDF as a smoke assertion, so a layout the native stack cannot produce is caught; see README.md.
The web components' rendered values, extracted per the README's .tabular contract. This is where 1's 'unchanged' claim is actually checked.
MenuBarTitle over the decoded summary, both display modes. The macOS client is a separate renderer with its own cache.
The sibling CLI renderer's format_amount, format_breakdown, and format_details output. This is the terminal surface where missing legacy money keys otherwise silently display as $0.00.
